headlines.article_text: JetBlue (JBLU) 3Q 2026 earnings Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points JetBlue Airways is in the middle of a plan that aims to cut costs and increase premium revenue. JetBlue shares are down more than 40% this month. In this article JBLU Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT JetBlue planes populate the tarmac on June 24, 2026 at JFK Airport in the Queens borough of New York City. Bruce Bennett | Getty Images JetBlue Airways reported a bigger loss in the third quarter compared with last year, but the New York carrier said strong travel demand is helping to offset higher fuel prices as it seeks to calm investors after shares fell to a new low Monday. JetBlue stock soared roughly 11% in after-hours trading Monday. JetBlue on Monday posted a net loss of $257 million for the three months ended Sept. 30, compared with a loss of $143 million a year earlier. The carrier's fuel bill rose 61% to $868 million. "Resilient demand and strong yields drove revenue well ahead of our initial expectations, allowing us to recapture more of the increase in fuel costs than we initially expected," CEO Joanna Geraghty said in an earnings release. "That momentum has carried into the fourth quarter, and Fort Lauderdale continues to deliver exceptional results even as we significantly grow capacity." JetBlue's average fares rose more than 19% to $245.11 in the third quarter from $205.67 in the year-earlier period. JetBlue executives are set to hold an earnings call on Tuesday at 10 a.m. ET, where they will face questions from analysts about the company's long-term health amid sustained losses. A group of the airline's senior creditors is reportedly working with restructuring adviser PJT Partners , the Wall Street Journal reported Friday. The carrier said it ended the quarter with $2.2 billion in liquidity and that its unencumbered asset base is now $7 billion, including $2.8 billion in aircraft and engines. JetBlue had total debt of $8.4 billion as of Sept. 30, the carrier said in its earnings filing Monday. "Importantly, we believe we have the liquidity and financing options to create a strong bridge to at least $1 EPS and positive free cash flow in 2028," CFO Ursula Hurley said in a statement. "We remain focused on disciplined cost execution and capital management as we work toward sustained profitability and positive free cash flow." Here is what JetBlue reported in the third quarter compared with Wall Street estimates compiled by LSEG: Loss per share: 60 cents adjusted vs. a loss of 55 cents expected Revenue: $2.81 billion vs. $2.82 billion expected JetBlue last posted an annual profit in 2019. The airline is in the middle of a multiyear turnaround plan that includes cutting cuts and boosting revenue by investing in premium seats, like a new domestic first class section that recently went on sale. Fuel costs have eaten into airline profits across the board. JetBlue said travel demand has remained strong despite higher fares , which are up more than 20% this year. JetBlue has struggled not just with higher costs but also with competition from larger rivals. It sought to acquire now-defunct carrier Spirit Airlines, but that deal was upended by a federal judge who ruled it was anticompetitive. A judge also blocked a regional partnership between JetBlue and American Airlines , which the airlines argued would help them compete better against carriers in the congested Northeast U.S. JetBlue now has a partnership with United Airlines . headlines.summary: Microsoft is trying to balance a rapid AI infrastructure build-out with capital efficiency.
headlines.article_text: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts as AI leads to efficiency push Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Around 60,000 Microsoft employees are eligible for the new buyout program across four countries, said a person familiar with the matter. The move comes six months after Microsoft announced its first-ever voluntary retirement program to a small set of U.S. workers. Employees must decide whether to take the offer in early December, and those participating will leave on Dec. 31. In this article MSFT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 1:40 01:40 Microsoft offering buyouts to some employees in U.S., Canada, India and U.K. Squawk on the Street Microsoft said Monday that it's offering buyouts to a wide swath of employees as it strives to balance a costly artificial intelligence infrastructure build-out with capital efficiency. The software maker announced a new voluntary exit offer for certain workers in the U.S., Canada, India and the United Kingdom at its experience level of 70 or below. Around 60,000 people are eligible, according to a person familiar with the matter, who asked not to be named while discussing an internal matter. The effort affects about 27% of Microsoft's total workforce of 223,000 people. Microsoft has been ramping up spending on data centers to accommodate high AI computing demand, supplying cloud services to Anthropic, OpenAI and a slew of other companies. Capital expenditures for the September quarter should exceed $50 billion, Microsoft said in July. In the same quarter a year ago, capital spending and finance leases came to $34.9 billion. That's put a strain on Microsoft's finances. In April, it announced a first-ever voluntary retirement program that around 7% of U.S. employees were eligible for. Then, in July, Microsoft announced plans to lay off 4,800 employees . "The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we're evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter," Amy Coleman, Microsoft's executive vice president and chief people officer, wrote in a memo to employees . "This builds on what we learned earlier this year through the Voluntary Retirement Program." Microsoft is in the midst of a business model transformation , increasingly trying to charge clients based on how much AI they actually use. It has armed programmers , sellers and supply chain workers with AI tools and observed noticeable results . At the same time, the 51-year-old maker of Windows and Office wants to ensure that it has the right talent to go after its most compelling new growth opportunities. The idea is to make the shift without weakening Microsoft's financial profile. In the second quarter, cloud rivals Alphabet and Amazon both reported negative free cash flow, but Microsoft showed $19.64 billion in positive free cash flow for the period, down 23% year over year. Some marketing, sales and engineering teams have decided not to participate in the new buyout, the person said. Employees must decide whether to take the offer in early December, and those participating will leave on Dec. 31, the person added. More than 30% of those who could join the voluntary retirement program went ahead with it, Microsoft said in July . But that was open to those at the senior director level and below, while the new initiative goes higher, to the vice president level, said the person briefed on the new plan. The person said Microsoft does not have a target in mind this time around. On Wednesday, Microsoft is scheduled to report third-quarter results.
